papers.abstract: Glioblastoma cells rely on connexin 43 (Cx43)‐based gap junctions (GJs) for intercellular communication, enabling them to integrate into a widely branched malignant network. Although there are promising prospects for new targeted therapies, the lack of clinically feasible GJ inhibitors has impeded their adoption in clinical practice. In the present study, we investigated tonabersat (TO), a blood–brain‐barrier‐penetrating drug with GJ‐inhibitory properties, in regard to its potential to disassemble intercellular connectivity in glioblastoma networks. Fluorescence‐guided measurements of calcein cell‐to‐cell transfer were used to study functional intercellular connectivity. Specific DNA fragmentation rates of propidium iodide‐stained nuclei were measured as a surrogate readout for cell death using flow cytometry. CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated gene editing of Cx43 served as a validation tool of cellular effects related to Cx43 GJ inhibition. 3′ mRNA sequencing was performed for molecular downstream analysis. We found that TO reduced intercellular GJ‐mediated cytosolic traffic and yielded a significant reduction of tumor microtube (TM) length. TO‐mediated inhibition of cellular tumor networks was accompanied by a synergistic effect for temozolomide‐induced cell death. CRISPR/Cas9 Cx43 ‐knockout revealed similar results, indicating that TO‐mediated inhibitory effects rely on the inhibition of Cx43‐based GJs. Gene set enrichment analyses found that GJ‐mediated synergistic cytotoxic effects were linked to a significant upregulation of cell death signaling pathways. In conclusion, TO disrupts TM‐based network connectivity via GJ inhibition and renders glioblastoma cells more susceptible to cytotoxic therapy. Given its previous use in clinical trials for migraine therapy, TO might harbor the potential of bridging the idea of a GJ‐targeted therapeutic approach from bench to bedside.

papers.abstract: Lipid metabolism is altered in rapidly proliferating cancer cells, where fatty acids (FAs) are utilized in the synthesis of sphingolipids and glycerophospholipids to produce cell membranes and signaling molecules. Receptor for activated C‐kinase 1 (RACK1; also known as small ribosomal subunit protein) is an intracellular scaffolding protein involved in signaling pathways. Whether such lipid metabolism is regulated by RACK1 is unknown. Here, integrated spatially resolved metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics revealed that accumulation of lipids in cervical cancer (CC) samples correlated with overexpression of RACK1 , and RACK1 promoted lipid synthesis in CC cells. Chromatin immunoprecipitation verified binding of sterol regulatory element‐binding protein 1 (SREBP1) to acetyl‐CoA carboxylase (ACC) and fatty acid synthase (FASN) promoters. RACK1 enhanced de novo FA synthesis by upregulating expression of sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor 1 ( SREBP1 ) and lipogenic genes FASN and ACC1 . Co‐immunoprecipitation and western blotting revealed that RACK1 interacted with protein kinase B (AKT) to activate the AKT/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)/SREBP1 signaling pathway to promote FA synthesis. Cell proliferation and apoptosis experiments suggested that RACK1‐regulated FA synthesis is key in the progression of CC. Thus, RACK1 enhanced lipid synthesis through the AKT/mTOR/SREBP1 signaling pathway to promote the growth of CC cells. RACK1 may become a therapeutic target for CC.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Recurrent and/or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck (R/M SCCHN) is a common cancer with high recurrence and mortality. Current treatments have low response rates (RRs). Methods Fifty-three patients with R/M SCCHN received continuous oral buparlisib. In parallel, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) were established in mice to evaluate resistance mechanisms and efficacy of buparlisib/cetuximab combination. Baseline and on-treatment tumour genomes and transcriptomes were sequenced. Based on the integrated clinical and PDX data, 11 patients with progression under buparlisib monotherapy were treated with a combination of buparlisib and cetuximab. Results For buparlisib monotherapy, disease control rate (DCR) was 49%, RR was 3% and median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were 63 and 143 days, respectively. For combination therapy, DCR was 91%, RR was 18% and median PFS and OS were 111 and 206 days, respectively. Four PDX models were originated from patients enrolled in the current clinical trial. While buparlisib alone did not inhibit tumour growth, combination therapy achieved tumour inhibition in three of seven PDXs. Genes associated with apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest were expressed at higher levels with combination treatment than with buparlisib or cetuximab alone. Conclusions The buparlisib/cetuximab combination has significant promise as a treatment strategy for R/M SCCHN. Clinical Trial Registration NCT01527877.

papers.abstract: Background: Treatment for B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) lasts >2 years and can impact families. The Children’s Oncology Group multicenter therapeutic trial AALL0932 randomized patients with NCI standard-risk, average-risk B-ALL (NCI-SR AR B-ALL) to receive maintenance vincristine/dexamethasone every 4 or 12 weeks (VCR/DEX4 or VCR/DEX12, respectively). Embedded in AALL0932, this study aimed to (1) longitudinally measure adverse family outcomes overall, and (2) determine whether patients on the VCR/DEX4 regimen (vs VCR/DEX12) had fewer adverse family outcomes. Methods: Patients with NCI-SR AR B-ALL who were offered enrollment on the multicenter randomized-controlled therapeutic trial AALL0932 were aged ≥4 years with an English-speaking parent. Parent-reported surveys were administered at T1–T5 (approximately 2, 9, 18, 26, and 38 months after diagnosis, respectively; T5 was assessed only in boys) and assessed household changes since leukemia diagnosis, leukemia-related household expenses in the past 4 weeks, unhealthy family functioning (Family Assessment Device score >2), and parents’ perceived child vulnerability (Child Vulnerability Scale ≥10). Postrandomization outcomes at T3 and T4 were compared between treatment groups using generalized linear mixed models and multivariable logistic regression models, as appropriate, adjusting for race and ethnicity. Results: Among 555 participants with completed evaluations, 420 were randomized (mean [SD] age, 6.0 [1.6] years; 45.7% female). At T1, 56.2% of randomized participants reported household changes since diagnosis (81.2% by T4), 88.6% reported ≥$100 in leukemia-related household expenses in the past 4 weeks (61.5% at T4), 19.0% had unhealthy family functioning (23.9% at T4), and 55.8% perceived their child as vulnerable (62.5% at T4). In multivariable models, VCR/DEX4 (vs VCR/DEX12) had an increased likelihood of reporting ≥$100 in leukemia-related expenses in the past 4 weeks (odds ratio, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.03–2.91), but other outcomes were similar between treatment arms. Conclusions: B-ALL family burdens develop early. Reducing maintenance VCR/DEX frequency may decrease expenses but not other outcomes. Interventions are needed to support families early and throughout ALL therapy.

papers.abstract: PURPOSE Updated analysis of phase I/II trials in recurrent/refractory (R/R) Ewing sarcoma (EwS) over the past 11 years. METHODS A systematic review was performed to identify phase I/II trials for R/R EwS in three databases (WHO, US National Library of Medicine, and European Clinical Trials Database) and/or published in PubMed/ASCO/European Society for Medical Oncology websites from 2014 to 2024. The search criteria included EwS OR bone sarcoma OR sarcoma AND Phase-I OR Phase-II. Eligibility and data extraction were performed independently by three reviewers, with priority given to trials with EwS specified data. Trials were categorized by therapeutic intervention, including targeted therapies, immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and combined therapies. RESULTS One hundred eight trials met inclusion criteria, predominantly academic (70%) and multicenter (81.5%), with significant US and European collaboration. Trial designs were mainly single-arm, with an increase in multiarm trials in the recent years and increased focus on the pediatric population. Trial modalities emphasized targeted therapies with tyrosine kinase, poly-ADP ribose polymerase, EWSR1::FLI1, and cell cycle inhibitors. Immunotherapy with monoclonal antibodies and CAR-T cells as primary agents is also under investigation. The COVID-19 pandemic coincided with a marked reduction in trial initiation in 2020. Among evaluable data, disease control rates averaged 44% and response rates 8%. CONCLUSION This review highlights evolving therapeutic directions in R/R EwS, with increased emphasis on targeted therapies and immunotherapies. Despite pandemic-related delays, trials have progressed in exploring novel targets, including EWSR1::FLI1 oncogenic fusion and DNA repair pathways. These findings underscore ongoing global efforts to address critical unmet needs in EwS treatment, offering a foundation for future trial designs, especially international, randomized phase‐II trials across all age ranges.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background The incidence of gastro-entero-pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) has increased, alongside novel therapies and care models. Whether these advances translated into improved survival is unclear. Methods Population-based retrospective cohort study of GEP-NENs between 2000–2019. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed using time-to-event methods. Restricted cubic splines assessed non-linear associations between diagnosis year and hazards of death; multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, primary site, and metastatic status. Results Among 9,420 patients, 5-year OS was 75.8% overall, 88.8% for non-metastatic disease, and 57.0% for metastatic disease. Mortality risk declined in more recent years, with diagnoses in 2013–2019 associated with lower hazards of death (adjusted HR 0.91, 95%CI 0.83–0.99). Improvements were confined to non-metastatic disease and to pancreas, stomach, and rectal primaries. Conclusion OS has modestly improved over two decades, largely reflecting stage migration rather than clear therapeutic gains. Advances that meaningfully improve survival in advanced GEP-NENs are needed.

papers.abstract: Abstract Radiotherapy (RT) transforms tumors into in situ vaccines that trigger antitumor immunity. However, the relevant pathways remain largely unelucidated, limiting clinical translation. Herein, we developed a hybrid dry-lab/wet-lab approach integrating systems-level immune phenotypes following homogenous or spatially fractionated RT (SFRT) with transcriptomic profiling of irradiated tumors. By combining feature extraction with machine-learning, including multilayer perceptron modeling, we ranked predictors of immune infiltration and patient survivability for each RT type. RT induced coordinated upregulation of viral RNA-binding proteins (OASes and RIG I-like receptors) along with endogenous retrovirus (ERV) RNAs predominately 400–800 bp long, which may serve as their ligands. During abscopal responses, OASes and ERV transcripts were co-induced and shared between irradiated and distant tumors. SFRT triggered earlier activation of OAS signaling versus homogenous RT. Our findings highlight ERVs as underappreciated contributors to RT-induced antitumor immunity and their interactions with intratumoral cytosolic sensors as potential novel biomarkers in precision radio-oncology.

papers.abstract: Abstract Patients with multiple myeloma accumulate hundreds of clinical documents over years of sequential therapy, and every treatment decision depends on synthesis across that history. Whether large language model–based systems can match expert agreement on this task, and where they fail, has not been established. On longitudinal records of 811 patients treated over 25 years (44,962 documents and 1,334,677 laboratory values), an agentic reasoning system guided by an indexed clinical skill library was compared against single-pass retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), iterative RAG, iterative RAG augmented with the same skill library, and full-context input on 469 expert-adjudicated patient-question pairs, with an exploratory cross-dataset evaluation on MIMIC-IV. The skill-guided agent exceeded the ceiling at which iterative RAG (75.7%) and full-context input (75.8%) converged, reaching 80.1% concordance, with its advantage widening on the most complex tasks (+11.2 percentage points) and longest records. Providing the same skill library to iterative RAG matched the agent in aggregate (79.0%) and on shorter records, whereas the agent retained a significant advantage on the longest records (+10.3 percentage points in the top decile, p = 0.017) and a numerical, non-significant advantage on the most complex questions (+5.4 percentage points). The aggregate error rate (12.2%) was comparable to expert disagreement (13.6%), but a higher proportion of system errors were clinically significant (57.8 versus 18.8%).

papers.abstract: Abstract Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is an aggressive malignancy of children, adolescents, and young adults driven by the EWS::FLI1 fusion oncoprotein with few effective treatment options in the relapsed or refractory setting. We validate six transmembrane epithelial antigen of the prostate 1 (STEAP1) as a fusion-regulated and clinically actionable surface antigen with broad expression across a series of primary EwS tumors. Analysis of EWS::FLI1 perturbation in EwS models demonstrated regulation of STEAP1 transcript and protein expression by oncogenic EWS::FLI1. Second-generation STEAP1 CAR T cells induced complete tumor regression in orthotopic models and exhibited dose-dependent activity in disseminated disease without evidence of antigen escape. Armoring STEAP1 CAR T cells with IL-18 further potentiated antitumor efficacy, achieving complete responses without overt toxicity in approximately 80% of mice at a five-fold lower cell dose where unarmored STEAP1 CAR T cells were ineffective. Notably, adoptive transfer of autologous STEAP1 CAR T cells is currently being evaluated in a first-in-human phase I/II clinical trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (NCT06236139) and the compelling preclinical data presented here support clinical translation to relapsed/refractory EwS.

papers.abstract: Abstract Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) have emerged as critical immune niches within the tumor microenvironment across various cancers. However, their structural organization and functional roles in non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) remain poorly characterized. In this study, we comprehensively characterized TLS in NMIBC using en bloc resected primary diagnostic specimens, which enabled high-resolution spatial mapping and quantitative histologic assessment across a large cohort of primary tumors (97 patients). Compared with TLS in inflammation-driven cystitis, tumor-associated TLS showed heterogeneous spatial organization, altered immune composition, and disrupted follicular dendritic cell (FDC) networks with reduced high endothelial venule density. TLS density increased with NMIBC grade and stage and correlated with higher recurrence risk and shorter progression-free survival in multivariable analysis. Paired analysis of primary and recurrent tumors showed a reduction in FDC density and a shift from M1 to M2 differentiation in tumor recurrences, suggesting the development of an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Single-nuclei RNA sequencing of TLS from NMIBC and cystitis samples revealed impaired germinal center activity in tumor-associated TLS, with asynchronous B-cell maturation and reduced B-cell interactions with both T follicular helper cells and FDC. Tumor-associated TLS also showed increased myeloid infiltration and altered dendritic cell function, including reduced MHC class II antigen presentation and downregulation of costimulatory (CD86–CD28) and migration-related (CD99) pathways compared with TLS from cystitis samples. Overall, we found that NMIBC-associated TLS are structurally and functionally impaired, which may limit effective local immune responses and suggests they may be relevant as biomarkers and targets for immunomodulatory therapy in bladder cancer.
